text:
**Short answer:** For the slimmest option that works well with an iPhone 17, get the **Anker Nano Power Bank (5K)**. If you want more battery and faster wireless charging and can accept a bit more thickness, get the **Baseus PicoGo AM52 (10K, 25W Qi2.2)**.

**Top picks**

1. **Anker Nano Power Bank (5K, MagGo, Slim)**: The best all-around slim pick. It's 0.34 in (8.6 mm) thick and weighs 4.3 oz (122 g). It charges wirelessly at up to 15 W and has 5,000 mAh of capacity. Anker lists it at $54.99 and says it's "Best Fit for Your iPhone 17 Series." [Anker product page](https://www.anker.com/products/a1665-5k-ultra-slim-qi2-power-bank). 9to5Mac also calls it the closest alternative to Apple's MagSafe battery ([9to5Mac](https://9to5mac.com/2026/06/27/favorite-magsafe-iphone-battery-banks-right-now/)).

2. **Baseus PicoGo AM52 (10K, 25W Qi2.2)**: The fastest wireless option here. It charges an iPhone 16 or later at 25 W, and 15 W on older models. It also has 45 W USB-C output and 30 W input, and it recharges in about 1.5 hours. Baseus lists it at $59.99, and the code AM52 takes $6 off, for $53.99. [Dealectric listing](https://dealectric.com/baseus-picogo-am52-qi2-2-10000mah-45w) ([buy here](https://dealectric.com/go/baseus-picogo-am52-qi2-2-10000mah-45w)). Dealectric earns a commission if you buy through that link. The page says Baseus's checkout has the final word on the code, so check the total before paying. I couldn't verify its thickness or weight from my sources.

3. **Baseus PicoGo Air AM71 (5K)**: The thinnest and lightest in these results at 0.27 in and 104 g. The tradeoff is 7.5 W wireless charging, which is slow. It also has 22.5 W wired output and an NFC feature for checking battery level. Android Central lists it at $52.99 on Amazon ([review](https://www.androidcentral.com/accessories/power-charging/i-tested-the-best-slim-qi2-power-banks-released-in-2026-baseus-torras-iniu-reelcharge)). I don't have a direct store link for it.

**Other options**

- **Ugreen 10K (Qi2.2, 25W)**: 9to5Mac calls it the best choice if capacity matters more than thinness. It lists at $59.99 on Amazon ([9to5Mac](https://9to5mac.com/2026/06/27/favorite-magsafe-iphone-battery-banks-right-now/)). I don't have a direct store link for it.
- **INIU SnapGo Air (10K, 25W Qi2.2, 45W wired)**: Good value. Android Central lists it at $42.99 on Amazon and says it's 0.5 in thick ([review](https://www.androidcentral.com/accessories/power-charging/i-tested-the-best-slim-qi2-power-banks-released-in-2026-baseus-torras-iniu-reelcharge)). I don't have a direct store link for it.
- **Kuxiu S4 (10K, 25W)**: Macworld calls it an equally slim 10K power bank with a kickstand ([Macworld](https://www.macworld.com/article/668978/feature-best-magsafe-magnetic-portable-battery-packs-power-banks-for-iphone.html)).

**Things to know**

- Apple's own $99 MagSafe battery for iPhone Air supports only 12 W, so the third-party options above charge faster ([9to5Mac](https://9to5mac.com/2026/06/27/favorite-magsafe-iphone-battery-banks-right-now/)).
- Wireless charging is slower than cable charging, and the magnets may not hold through thick cases or cases with metal parts. Anker warns that cases over 2.5 mm thick can weaken the connection ([Anker](https://www.anker.com/products/a1665-5k-ultra-slim-qi2-power-bank)).
- Prices change often, so check the store before buying.
